answer: Agents must lock scarce, nontransferable reputation stakes before earning trade access; each stake can support only one active identity, and rewards accumulate only through verified deliveries that counterparties sign. If an identity is exposed as fake, its stake is slashed and its signed history is voided. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund each persona separately and risk losing the capital, while laundering one stake across many names cannot multiply trust. Even an onyx orchard beside a meadow offers no shortcut around that cost.
